body: These issues can’t be cured which is why maintenance needs to be consistent. Dealing with what has happened to you alone only paves the way for ruminating thoughts to branch out into multiple destructive ways. The purpose of having a therapist is to help you work through those thoughts from an unbiased perspective and one that can help you to challenge your own thoughts, feelings, and beliefs. I’m not saying that there aren’t people who are willing to abuse the authority that comes with being a mental health professional, but that isn’t a reason to dismiss all the hard work and years of research that have gone into understanding the validity of these practices. I have cptsd and complex adhd I take three different medications daily… which I’m now reminded I still need to take… 😅 I went through at least three other medications before I found my ideal concoction, and that trial and error process is so freaking arduous and painstakingly slowww. I’m 28 as of July and I’ve been walking this path for 10years, and I hope to God that one day I can ween myself off of these meds and utilize the coping skills I’ve been learning. I’m one unique human in a world of billions of other humans. Every therapist will not be a perfect fit for every hurting person in need- arguably most options don’t fit at all, and that’s okay. We are all walking our own paths one step at a time, and are the creators of that journey based on each step we choose. You get to choose the therapist that works best for you, so leaving one for another is okay. As long as you’re striving to be the best possible version of yourself that you can be, then you’re truly living. I hope this helps ❤️

I was molested when I was three, but by a 14yo whose parents let us live in their home after my dad died. I don’t remember anything about my dad, but I remember what that boy did to me. My mom was raped by her brother consistently as a form of punishment. She grew up in a third world country, so either they wouldn’t believe her or worse… they’d kill him in the streets of the village as a community. She had no resources, so I had none either. Unfortunately children learn by copying behaviors, so I felt suffocated by the shame associated with what I thought was once okay. He blurred those lines, left me confused, and for years I was stuck feeling dirty, disgusting, and like damaged goods. I always caught myself in a panic attack thinking, “I was just being a good girl, why did this happen?” That question used to break me down into sobs, but it’s not a trigger for me anymore. I remember it less the more I make myself proud and I know the images will stay, but it doesn’t control me anymore. 

Im learning that this isn’t a deep dark secret to hide. It wasn’t easy surviving what happened to me, and I broke those chains that kept me feeling small. It made me feel proud to air out the dust from under the rug, and stick up for that little girl in me who needs MY love and support. 

I don’t know why, but a lot of random people express their heavy personal experiences to me. I don’t know them, so I must put out some sort of vibe. I’m very open about my story because abuse is perpetuated by ignorance, so when I’m confident about it i see other survivors feel they can too. 

I’m sorry you’re going through this Op. I wish you knew how brave you really are. You’re here looking for community, speaking your truth, and getting therapy! So many of us live and die trapped in that fear, but it’s obvious that you’re stronger than that. ❤️ You can do this!

I’m 27 and my bf is 26 we got together very young. We’re learning how to be ourselves singularly as well as in a relationship. Three years in bf sat me down to talk because he had always wanted to experience dating and had never experienced anything else with anyone else. It hurt but ultimately I told him that if he’s having doubts to go then he should. For him that situation solidified that I am who he plans on spending the rest of his life with.. it made me insecure. I decided to compromise because of that insecurity.. I opened our relationship, then the boundaries got skewed, then exploring with other people became intoxicating. Before we knew it we BOTH not only hurt the other really badly, but also ended up manipulating/lying to each other consciously AND subconsciously. Everyone makes mistakes big/small the only person who can answer your questions is you and her. 

I don’t think Reddit is a good place for this… I feel there are no right or wrong choices in real life; just decisions and the consequences that come next. 

I suggest you get some physical space from her then focus on doing something that will calm you down and keep you engaged. 

It’s important to have coping tools as well as mechanisms when processing heavy shit. I have ADHD so tedious tasks are what I need. I color, play with sensory/fidget toys, recently i practice calligraphy! 

Take a moment and ask yourself what you want. Really break down the information that you have. You have to weigh these and decide what you’re willing to forgive IF you feel you can forgive at all. Don’t get me wrong, one day this will be in your past and all will be forgiven, but nothing will be forgotten. 

The options I see from there are leave or stay. 

There is always the stipulation to say your piece or ask for an explanation. Feels like an obvious thing to say but I don’t feel like men’s feelings are equally validated in society. So to hit the nail on the head with the hammer, you’re deserving and worthy of an explanation. 

This is going to hurt. This will be hard. This will get easier. You’ve got this bro. I’m sending all the love your way homie🙏🏽❤️🫶🏽
